thesis: Buy the new note at auction - where dealers are paid to absorb supply - and sell it on the fifth session after issue, when the concession has typically been given back. The entry price is the Treasury's printed auction price and the exit is the par curve's own mark, so the trade's two ends are both official numbers.
drivers: Best trade: 3-Year 91282CPP0 (long, primary-auction to secondary-curve) 2025-12-08 to 2025-12-16 for $1,647.15.
Worst trade: 10-Year 91282CNS6 (primary-auction to secondary-curve) 2025-09-18 to 2025-11-28 for $-5,781.25.
14 of 31 closed trades made money; coupons paid $0.00 and financing cost $-26,820.26.

Official par curve over the window: 3-month 4.02% -> 4.14% (+12 bp), 2-year 3.52% -> 4.74% (+122 bp), 10-year 4.06% -> 5.01% (+95 bp), 30-year 4.66% -> 5.35% (+69 bp). Duration exposures are paid off against this path.
